## 🎓 Today's lesson
- **What is an Offer for Sale (OFS) in an IPO?**
  When a company launches an Initial Public Offering (IPO), the money raised can go to two different places. In a **Fresh Issue**, the company issues brand-new shares, and the cash goes directly onto the company's balance sheet to fund new factories, buy equipment, or pay off corporate debt. In an **Offer for Sale (OFS)**, existing shareholders (like founders, government parents, or venture capital funds) sell their own shares to the public. The company itself gets **zero new money** from an OFS; all proceeds go straight to the sellers. For example, in the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO, 100% of the ₹8,100 crore raised went to its parent company Coal India, not into Mahanadi's bank account. [[Bloomberg.com]](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxNUkxRd1B0NXpiTm5KM1FTeU9aQVRoV3prVFlLX3NhR0RIZUllYVdtelZzMWUwZWwtRVVUY2Z0aFVKeElIZW9HWVY2bHZ0YkZkRU1rVU5nR0JmSmQ4TTRuTnBEenVxRzFxSDhveUtIWWVjZ0twZ2NlbmxnbE5WSWxTSzlpd210LVFrVnUxYU9RcGtYWm1Za1JrRHJzZDRWbGF5c0gyMm1tTlptbzJZdTRfeWdRNA?oc=5) Knowing the split between Fresh Issue and OFS helps you understand whether you are funding future company growth or helping early investors cash out.

## 🌱 Good news
- **Community gifts a new car to woman who feeds thousands:** For 37 years, Gloria Kennard cooked Thanksgiving dinners for her local community in Texas, serving over 2,000 people annually. This year, the town quietly raised over $27,000 to surprise "Miss Gloria" with a brand-new car to thank her for decades of selfless service.
